Noindex tag

You really can't stop them. Robots.txt is probably the most ignored thing on the internet.
Google obeys robots.txt and it holds a majority share of search engine activity. It's not leak-proof, but it is generally effective.

Umm... No. It's not. Most reputable search engines honor the robots.txt file (which is what this topic is about... search indexing). I'd argue that the sitemap documents are the most ignored thing on the internet.

Just look at the end of the OP's link. "Google's main indexing spider, Googlebot, is not known to recognize any of these techniques." Although it's been a couple of years, I've personally seen Google ignoring robots.txt in my own web logs.
I'm sorry, but I know for a fact that Google's indexing spider does respect robots.txt, because I manage a web server and have watched it respect it. "noindex" is not the same as "robots.txt."
There's also a chance that it wasn't googlebot breaking the rules, but rather someone using the googlebot user agent. I've used it sometimes to get past annoying ad-click walls.
What's more likely is that the person had the TLD in the robots.txt which will make it ignore the file because it can't index a TLD if it's listed, so assumes it's a faulty file.
Even if some bad actors ignore robots.txt, why shouldn’t we use the tools available? Set it anyway.

maybe someone could do some kind of light encoding of the text when the referal is not correct (e.g. your own website) that way robots would scourge your website but only retrieve garbage data.

dunno if ever feasible.
I’m for this. Only content in public subs needs to be indexed (if you want to drive traffic to the site). Meta pages like user profiles don’t benefit from being indexed.
